subject: Temporary retention window request — EU PCI investigation
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@finport.com>
To: jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 11 Jun 2028 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: Request: temporary retention slice for EU PCI investigation

Hi Jordan,

We're in the middle of a time-sensitive PCI investigation and our internal auditors have asked for a short-term window of raw request logs and KV cache snippets tied to a small set of user sessions (customer IDs attached in the questionnaire). Our compliance team needs the data preserved for up to 10 days to reproduce a suspected payment flow anomaly.

Can Redwood provide a timeboxed exception to the standard EU retention policy (we currently have automatic deletion at 72 hours for these ephemeral traces)? We only need a narrow slice (approx 4GB) and we are happy to sign an explicit data handling addendum or escrow the evidence via your secure transfer.

Attachments: pci_evidence_request.pdf (PDF)

Suggested next steps from our side:
- Quick confirmation of feasibility
- Preservation window (requested): 10 days starting 2028-06-11
- Secure delivery instructions once preserved

Thanks,
Elena Morales

Folks — forwarding a live request from FinPort. They're asking for a 10-day hold on a small set of ephemeral traces in our EU cluster to support a PCI audit.

Key constraints:
- Scope: specific session IDs (list in the attached questionnaire)
- Size: ~4GB
- Region: EU (data residency is required)
- Duration requested: 10 days starting today

I'm looking for (1) a quick read on whether this is feasible without violating our EU data residency controls, (2) a proposed minimal process (audit trail, access restrictions), and (3) an approval path so we can respond to the customer this afternoon.

Attachments: pci_evidence_request.pdf

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call.
— Jordan

Jordan / Neha —

Quick notes from legal/compliance POV before we commit:
- Any exception must be time-boxed, auditable, and restricted to named Redwoods staff and a named FinPort contact.
- We need FinPort to sign the Data Handling Addendum (DHA) and a one-page non-repudiation acceptance confirming they will not request additional slices beyond the stated session IDs.
- Prefer that preserved material be staged to an S3 bucket in the EU region with encryption and limited IAM role access; we should not change cluster-level deletion policies globally.

Neha — do you see any red flags from security (access model + SSO proofs) if we do a 10-day slice? If not, I'll draft the DHA and a short internal approval note for exec sign-off.

Laura Bennett
Head of Sales Ops (acting) | Redwood Inference
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 16:41:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: temporary retention slice for EU PCI investigation

Laura / Jordan —

Security sign-off provided with conditions below. I've validated the requested session identifiers against the EU cluster and confirmed the size estimate (~4GB). My conditions:

1) Timebox: 7 days (not 10) starting 2028-06-11 09:00 UTC — this limits exposure and still gives FinPort auditors time to reproduce.
2) Storage: stage preserved artifacts to a dedicated, encrypted EU-S3 bucket (retention TTL = 7 days) with access via a short-lived IAM role (max 24-hour tokens). No direct access to underlying node disks.
3) Audit trail: every access must be recorded; Redwoods staff list limited to: neha_kapoor, vivek_kulkarni, laura_bennett, jordan_blake. Any FinPort downloads must be via a signed, single-use expiring link.
4) Legal: FinPort must sign the DHA and confirm they accept the limited window and scope.

I approve the carveout under these constraints. Jordan — please relay to Elena and attach the DHA. I'll generate the secure bucket and a one-time access token once the DHA is executed.

Attachments (for internal trace): syslog_excerpt.tar.gz (archive, 3.9GB)

Neha Kapoor
